Library-best bulk concept: o pieces on row 1 (o_row1), score 0.62, partial.
It also responds to the rare odd-row threat flag for o (100 training positions), which the concept sweep ranks first (score 0.94) but which covers too few positions to read the unit by.
An ad-hoc reading, the negative of x's open twos plus x on b1, c1, d1 and e1, scores 0.67 (partial) and is stored as its meaning.
A gate that lowers x's predicted chance when c3 is x: on for 15368 of 54045 positions.
In the probe sweep it is off with c3 blank or o and reads 1.72 with x at c3; an o at e2 also switches it on (0.79).
On the data it is on for 4933 of the 5498 positions with x at c3.

Its weight into the logit is negative, yet positions with x at c3 are won more often (78.7% against 64.4% for the rest): the gate is a correction to the direct terms and the raising gates, not a sign that c3 is bad for x; in the sweep the whole-model chance still rises from 58% with c3 blank to 94%
A positional gate on single cells (c3, e2, c1, d3, f1, b2), described by its formula (attached); concept c_c3 scores 0.41 (closed form only).
The sweep-first concept, x having a threat, scores 0.68 but holds on 660 positions.
The rule 'x at c3' scores 0.78 (partial) and is stored as its meaning.
In the probe sweep its value goes from 0.21 with no x in the centre to 5.32 with four; an o at d2 switches it off (0.00) while an x there raises it to 1.71.

It enters the logit with a positive weight, so x's centre pieces raise the predicted chance through this part; in the whole model the sweep's chance rises from 58% with no centre piece to 87% with four.
On the data it is on for 31176 of 54045 positions (outcome rate 73.0% against 56.1% for the rest) and for 86.8% of the 21388 positions where x has at least one centre piece.
Concept centre_x scores 0.64 (partial): the centre count sets most of its value, and the cells c1, c2, b2 and d3 adjust it.
The sum of the centre count and x at d2 scores 0.75 (partial) and is stored as its meaning.
A small gate, on for 7121 of 54045 positions, with a positive weight into the logit.
Its bulk behaviour is positional: an x at g3 switches it on (0.57 in the sweep; off with g3 blank or o), and x at e2, d3, e3, f3 or o at c2, d4, e1, a6 raise it.

The threat reading is fitted to 66 rows, so the unit is stored as a positional gate: concept c_g3 scores 0.37 (closed form only); the sweep-first concept, the odd-row threat flag, scores 1.00.
The rule 'x at g3' scores 0.63 (partial) and is stored as its meaning.
A weak-position gate that lowers x's predicted chance: on for 29176 of 54045 positions, whose outcome rate is 55.2% against 78.3% for the rest.

It is on when x has no piece in the centre column and few open twos: in the sweeps it reads 0.90 with no x in the centre and is off from one centre piece upward, and it falls from 1.47 at zero open twos for x to off at three.
On the data it is on for 31.4% of the 21388 positions with an x centre piece, against 68.8% of the 32657 without one.
Concept x_open_2 (gate on when the count is low) scores 0.53 (partial).
It also fires on the 66 positions with an odd-row threat for x (sweep-first concept, score 0.99), too few to read it by.
A positional gate with a positive weight, on for 14084 of 54045 positions (outcome rate 80.1% against 60.8% for the rest).

It switches on when c3 is x (0.94 in the sweep; off with c3 blank or o) and is raised by x on the bottom row at b1, c1, d1 and a1 and by o at f1, g1 and e1, and lowered by o's pieces in the centre column; b1 alone barely moves it (0.03 with x there).
On the data it is on for 3085 of the 5498 positions with x at c3.
No library concept reads it: concept c_c3 scores 0.26 (closed form only); described, not explained.
A gate that lowers x's predicted chance when x has few open twos: on for 37604 of 54045 positions, whose outcome rate is 59.6% against 80.2% for the rest.
In the sweep its value falls from 2.11 at zero open twos for x to off at four, and an x at e1 raises it (2.75 against 0.25 with o there).
On the data it is on for 5518 of the 11336 positions with three or more open twos for x.
Concept x_open_2 scores 0.33 (closed form only): the open-two count sets its slope but single cells (e1, c3, e3, a4, b2, e2, e4) set its level, so it is a positional gate.
It also fires on the 100 positions with an odd-row threat for o (sweep-first concept, score 0.95), too few to read it by.
A positional gate with a positive weight, on for 34275 of 54045 positions.

It switches on when c3 is o (1.95 in the sweep; off with x there) and then grows with x's open ones and open twos: with o at c3 its value rises from 0.00 at zero open ones for x to 1.72 at eight, while the whole-model chance rises from 1% to 38%.
On the data it is on for 5545 of the 6162 positions with o at c3.
Concept x_open_1 scores 0.10 (closed form only); the gate's level is set by the cells c3, c1, b2, c2, b1, a1 and g1, so it is a positional gate, described, not explained.
The rule 'o at c3' scores 0.51 (partial) and is stored as its meaning.
A bottom-row positional gate with a positive weight, on for 9743 of 54045 positions (outcome rate 81.8% against 62.3% for the rest).

It needs x at c1 together with o on the bottom row at b1, g1 or a1: with x at c1 and o at b1, the sweep reads 1.40 with o at g1, 0.40 with g1 blank and off with x there, and the whole-model chance goes from 91% to 68%.
On the data, 7970 of its 9743 acting positions have x at c1.
No library concept reads it: concept c_c1 scores 0.46 (closed form only); described, not explained.

The sum of the centre count, x at d2 and x at b3 scores 0.72 (partial) and is stored as its meaning.

The concept sweep ranks the rare threat flags first for several units (for example unit4 with the odd-row threat for x, score 1.00), but those flags hold on 66 (x, odd row) and 100 (o, odd row) training positions, so they were not stored as the units' meanings.

Unit1 is an offset on 46681 of 54045 positions that shrinks as x's position improves and unit10 a large term that caps the centre column's positive effect; both are compensating terms whose purpose is visible against the direct sum rather than as a game concept on their own.
